title: Why poverty is rising in America — TikTok
notes: Hook question: why did poverty jump more in one year than ever before? Answer, built scene by scene: pandemic aid like the expanded Child Tax Credit expired, inflation raised the bar, and the pain landed hardest in California, the Florida panhandle and the Mississippi Delta, even for people who work. The close names the fix from the article: expand the EITC and CTC.

Figures are from the article (Oct 4, 2023, 2022 Census SPM data) and the sources it cites. The news card is the Census Bureau's Sep 2026 report; its line says only that poverty hasn't returned to the 2021 low (SPM 12.9% in 2023 and 2024, 13.1% in 2025). Solo post, so the narration uses 'I'.

post.headline: Why poverty jumped faster than ever
post.caption: In 2022 the U.S. poverty rate saw its largest one-year increase in history, and child poverty more than doubled. When the expanded Child Tax Credit expired, the gains vanished, and poverty has never returned to its 2021 low.
post.cta: Full story and interactive maps at the link in bio.

say: 35 million Americans live in poverty, a rate that has remained stubbornly high since the pandemic.
Even child poverty, which more than doubled in 2022 from 5.2% to 12.4%, has stayed above 13% for the last 3 years.
I looked at where poverty lives, why it rose so quickly, and why it hasn't fallen back to historical levels.

cues.text: 35 million Americans live in poverty, a rate that has remained stubbornly high since the pandemic.
Even child poverty, which more than doubled in 2022 from 5.2% to 12.4%, has stayed above 13% for the last 3 years.
I looked at where poverty lives, why it rose so quickly, and why it hasn't fallen back to historical levels.
Pandemic aid like the expanded Child Tax Credit pushed poverty to record lows, and when it expired the gains vanished.
Research shows child poverty would have been 50% lower in 2022 if the expanded credit had stayed.
Inflation raised the bar too, since the poverty line for a family of four jumped nearly 10% to $34,518.
Where you live matters. California has the highest poverty rate of any state because affordability is so bad. Florida has the second worst because opportunity is so low.
In Gadsden County on the Florida panhandle, one in four people live in poverty, and two in five children do.
Demographics also shape the divide. In Mississippi, Black residents are three times more likely to live in poverty than White residents.
In Tunica County, MS, 68% of Black families live in poverty, compared to 12% of White families.
A job isn't always enough to lift someone out of poverty, since 6.3 million people in poverty work full-time.
Some industries have much higher poverty than others. In California, frontline fast food workers earn about $16,800 a year, just 27% of what workers in other industries make.
Once lawmakers let the pandemic era benefits expire, poverty has floated well above its 2021 lows.
The EITC and Child Tax Credit lifted 10.6 million people above the poverty line, and we now have clear evidence that expanding these programs would bring poverty down.
You can read the full story on American Inequality.
